title: Span collapsed-state design criteria & interaction notes
content:
Purpose:
- Capture interaction decisions and acceptance criteria for a compact / collapsed span state in the trace viewer. This doc is a working sketch for PM/Design/Eng grooming; not final.

High level goals:
- Surface signal-dense traces without overwhelming vertical real estate.
- Let users quickly scan large traces (100s of spans) and still jump to relevant detail.
- Preserve keyboard + screen-reader access; ensure collapsed view is not just visual.
- Provide smooth transitions (no jarring reflows) and safe perf for traces with many spans.

Problem statements / evidence:
- Large traces currently require a lot of scrolling and users lose context when expanding multiple spans. (User interviews 10/2024 + support tickets TRACE-34, TRACE-67)
- Observability customers often want a "condensed" view in incident triage to find top latency contributors quickly.
- Existing waterfall compacting (density reduction) loses metadata like error indicators and annotations. Need to preserve at-a-glance signals.

User scenarios to support:
1) Pager duty: on-call engineer in a noisy incident opens a 400-span trace, needs to find first 3 suspects in <2 minutes.
2) Performance audit: infra engineer comparing two traces to spot changes in tail-latency.
3) Developer local debugging: wants to expand only spans that correspond to their service or correlation id.

Design constraints / non-goals:
- Non-goal: fully redesigning trace model (we keep current span tree model).
- Must work with existing span tags, annotations, and span grouping (service-level collapse).
- The collapsed state must be renderable without server-side transformation (client-side collapse).
- Animations must be toggleable for low-power or low-performance devices.

Key UX proposals (sketch descriptions):
A) Collapsed span tile (default compact row)
- Height: 28px (vs current 40px) with tight typography.
- Left: service color band + small service initials chip (2–3 chars) for fast scanning.
- Middle: compact span name (ellipsis) + tiny chips for status (error/warn) and latency bucket (p50/p95 icon).
- Right: visual miniature timeline (sparkline) representing span duration relative to trace; hover expands to full timeline popover.
- Hit target: entire row clickable; secondary actions via right-edge kebab.

B) Context peek on hover / keyboard focus
- Tooltip/popover that surfaces top 3 attributes: span id, host, and any error message. Popover is non-modal and dismisses on mouseout or blur.
- Keyboard: focus on row and press Space to open context peek; Enter to open full span panel.

C) Span grouping + smart collapse rules
- By default collapse leaf spans whose sibling count > 8 into a grouped "n spans" node. Group node shows aggregated duration (max/avg) and error count.
- Provide quick filter chips: "group by service", "group by span name", "group by status" (persisted in user settings).

D) Progressive expansion / lazy detail loading
- Expand is client-side. When a user expands a grouped node, render immediate children collapsed then progressively animate to final heights.
- For extremely large traces we show a loading shimmer for details that require extra decoding (rare) — design to avoid layout jumps.

E) Sticky mini-detail panel (right rail)
- When a span is selected, instead of pushing content and causing reflow, open a sticky right rail with full details, stackable for multiple quick pins. Pins persist during session.

Micro-interactions and animation spec:
- Row expand/collapse: 120ms ease-out height transition.
- Hover popover: 80ms fade-in with 4px translateY.
- Grouping reveal: 160ms staggered reveal for up to first 12 children, additional children appear instantly to avoid long animations.
- Motion toggle: user setting "Reduced motion for trace UI" disables transitions and uses instant show/hide.

Keyboard & accessibility notes:
- Each span row must be focusable (role="listitem"). Use aria-expanded on grouped nodes.
- Popover content should be reachable via F6-like navigation and read by screen readers (announce: "Span collapsed, press enter to open details").
- Ensure color band has text labels for color-blind users; rely on icons + text.
- Provide a "compact mode" preference persisted in profile (helps screen-reader users opt in/out).

Filtering & discoverability interactions:
- When applying route/route-id filter, offer "collapse unrelated services" toggle to auto-collapse spans not matching filter.
- Inline filter pill suggestions: hovering over a service in the left band shows a quick "hide others" button.

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets, priority, rough points):
- TRACE-310: Implement compact row UI + style tokens (P0, 5 points)
- TRACE-311: Grouped node aggregation logic (P0, 8 points)
- TRACE-312: Sticky right rail span detail (P1, 8 points)
- TRACE-313: Keyboard nav + ARIA states for collapsed rows (P1, 5 points)
- TRACE-314: Reduced motion toggle and perf tests for 1000-span traces (P0, 3 points)
- TRACE-315: Hover popover accessible variant for touch devices (P2, 3 points)

Engineering considerations / perf guardrails:
- Virtualization: reuse existing virtual scroller. Compact rows reduce visible height but can increase row count rendered; ensure windowing works correctly.
- DOM nodes: prefer single-row DOM with CSS for reduced state instead of full-detailed nodes hidden with display:none; helps memory.
- JS overhead: grouping computation should be O(n) pass with threshold early-exit; avoid expensive tree walks on every frame.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should grouping be on by default for traces > X spans? (proposal: enable auto-group for traces > 200 spans).
- Do we store user preference server-side or in local storage? (prefers server-side for cross-device consistency but heavier to implement).
- How aggressive should auto-collapse be for traces with heavy fan-out? Need empirical rules from telemetry.

Design alternatives we rejected (quick rationale):
- Completely compressed heatmap-only rows: loses per-span metadata & actions so rejected for triage workflows.
- Server-side collapsed representation (precomputed groups): increases backend complexity and reduces interactivity.

Acceptance criteria (QA checklist):
- Compact rows render with correct tokens at 28px height on chrome/firefox/safari.
- Grouped node correctly reports count and aggregated duration within +/-5% of client compute.
- Keyboard + screen reader announce collapsed state and allow expansion.
- No regressions in trace load time for traces under 200 spans; large traces show <2s degrade measured in CI.

Next steps (owners and rough timeline):
- Design: produce final Figma frames for compact row variants + popover states (Evelyn, 2 weeks).
- Frontend: spike grouping algorithm + virtualization edge-case checklist (Marco, 1 week).
- Backend: telemetry event design to count trace sizes and fan-out (Diego, 1 week).
- Schedule grooming: include TRACE-310..315 in next planning board for sprint starting 2025-01-20.

Notes to reviewers:
- I'm leaning toward server-persisted compact-mode preference but want eng input on infra cost.
- See linked figma for pixel-level spacing; the figma has 3 density variants (ultra, compact, normal) — recommend delivering compact + normal for MVP.
- If we want to demo at the weekly product sync, I'll prepare a click-through with toggles for grouping and reduced motion.

Scratchpad / quick sketches (text):
- "service band" | span name .................. | mini-timeline | kebab
- grouped node: chevron down • 12 spans • max: 200ms • errors: 2
- keyboard flow: Tab to row -> Space opens peek -> Enter opens rail -> P toggles pin

End of doc.
